# Final campaign: phase-filtered JFR investigation

Runtime `334234c24e9008f4a2614b8213b8b2e73b6ba9e1`. All four measured commands terminated before this offline analysis. One Java reader ran at a time, with a 768 MiB or 1536 MiB heap. No analyzer was rerun. No heap dumps exist, so retained-owner attribution is unavailable.

## Phase totals

All ten requested windows are covered by the observed JFR event range; Stirling run-30/31 did not need a run-16 fallback. GB below means 10⁹ bytes. ## Three distinct later-run bottlenecks

Conductor run-12 BACKWARD takes 375.681 s; run-13 FORWARD takes 71.532 s. In run-12, complete loop observation accounts for 67.91% of Java CPU samples and 64.96% of allocation weight. C2 initial lookup is 47.59% CPU / 26.84% allocation; C5 is 4.40% / 4.55%. The prior broad DemandStore class probe mixed C2 and C5; the final consumer uses operation-specific probes. In run-13, C2 is only 2.63% / 2.41%, while C5 is 19.01% / 12.79% and TAINT canonicalization is 40.90% / 41.76%. The backward slowdown has substantial repeated complete-family C2 work; not every slow phase has the same mechanism.

Stirling run-30 BACKWARD takes 39.060 s; run-31 FORWARD takes 1.234 s. The backward hotspot is FlowGroup canonicalization: 89.19% CPU / 84.70% allocation, mainly subtractSubsumed (84.99% / 77.10%), under ScopedEdgeStore admission. Loop observation is only 2.01% / 4.06%. SubtractKey allocates an estimated 27.05 GB and Integer 20.38 GB. Saved full stacks pass through ScopedEdgeStore.addPacket → ConclusionGroup.addAll → FlowGroup.addAll → subtractSubsumed → FlowAlgebra.subtract. Run-31 has only 63 Java samples, so its percentage estimates have low resolution.

Pinned 52829 FlowGroup.add worked on the offered pending row. Current addAll additionally canonicalizes every retained header against all other headers, repeats for MUST overlap/fill, makes another full canonical pass, and compares against all previous headers. It does this even when insert returns no fresh change. The selected canonical laws must remain, but unchanged canonical owners should not need unrelated full rescans. This is a current implementation work-amplification candidate, not evidence that subsumption semantics must be rolled back.

## Thingsboard run-1 has two expensive phases

Reported engine time is 521.169 s, joined static binding 292.711 s, and marker envelope 813.880 s. The approximate pre-binding window allocates 2,719.53 GB. Ordinary call initial replay accounts for 26.38% CPU / 30.69% allocation, DATA delivery 21.28% / 27.01%, Target delivery 3.56% / 4.01%. The complete summary pub/sub family is 66.12% / 77.06%. Synchronous pool-runtime frames alone do not explain this work, but statics can enqueue work whose later stack no longer contains the pool. No static-versus-nonstatic payload percentage is inferred from stack names.

FlowBackedSummaries is 28.65% CPU / 30.89% allocation; diagonal admission is 18.91% / 22.82%; diagonal scalar projection is 3.91% / 4.04%. Saved stacks include both ordinary delivery and block DATA delivery → run1Cover → block completion admission → DiagonalRelations → temporary TaintGroup. Scoped stores, summary stores and publication owners are distinct; do not assign every FlowBackedSummaries frame to publication. The pinned diagonal-source comparison documents that full per-mark/class projection reconstruction became unconditional in this iteration, including duplicates. Qualifying duplicate rates and projection sizes are not measured, so that candidate has no asserted speedup.

The derived joined-binding window allocates another 780.24 GB. OwnedJoinedStaticWriterBinding is 97.57% CPU / 97.39% allocation; native mark selection is 20.10% / 29.60%. Top allocation stacks pass through complete → satisfying → satisfyingPart → markSubPart → mapLeaves/walkNodes. Its native receipt records 2,969,858 processed writers, 462,365,666 candidate inputs, 33,190,272 matches and 33,099,986 bound outputs. duplicateInputs=0 only describes the per-writer visited-key set. It does not prove that distinct writer conclusions never repeat the same owner/premise input match. Grouping compatible writer work could reuse matching, but repeated-premise multiplicity is still unmeasured.

Thingsboard after-GC maxima are 15.66 GB before binding and 15.70 GB in binding (about 14.6 GiB under a 16 GiB JVM cap). This shows substantial live pressure without proving a leak or its owner. No dump was captured. Periodic maxMemory-freeMemory logs are not used as heap-used measurements.

## Run-1 construction differs across projects

| Run-1 project | Forms payload CPU / allocation | Call-plan build CPU / allocation | Alias build CPU / allocation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| OWASP | 48.02% / 42.51% | 41.98% / 39.83% | 19.87% / 9.82% |
| conductor | 61.66% / 47.66% | 41.87% / 37.46% | 28.63% / 29.42% |
| Stirling-PDF | 73.45% / 58.48% | 41.03% / 31.38% | 30.89% / 22.57% |

These are first-use construction/access stacks, not proof of repeated soft-cache rebuilds. JIRCallPlanBuilder computes aliases(back) before the runtime MemoryEffect guard. Avoiding unused construction is a separate source-backed question; preserve rule-condition alias clients, backward alias semantics and static effects. Do not promote this cost to the dominant Thingsboard issue: its pre-binding FormsCache share is only 5.72% CPU / 2.11% allocation.

## Portable evidence and proof boundaries

Each `*-jfr.json` contains weighted totals, allocation classes, top 100 complete CPU/allocation stacks, exact inclusive probes, GC observations and per-second bins. Each metadata file pins JFR/log/manifest/summary/consumer/wrapper hashes, requested window and latest iteration labels. `jfr-review-summary.json` combines metrics and pins the relevant runtime sources. `jfr-review-receipt.json` records the sequential reader run and bounded heap per reader. Oversized debug lines are drained in bounded chunks, and skipped oversized workload records are counted.

The evidence supports different operation-removal targets: complete-family loop query reuse for Conductor; incremental canonical owner updates for Stirling; diagonal projection and repeated ordinary summary work plus joined writer matching for Thingsboard. None of these samples alone proves an infinite loop, exact duplicate-key rate, a guaranteed speedup or a retained-memory owner. Changes must preserve both H memberships, complete C2 companions, all physical scopes/ports and source/Target permissions.

The highest weighted core stack is **internal block DATA delivery into completion
storage**, rather than a method-summary publication stack:

```text

  -> applySummaryPart -> run1CoverFacts
```

`Entry.addCompletion` deduplicates results before routing them onward. In run-1,

The visible canonical cost is therefore real completion admission. Calling every

A second saved pipeline is **ordinary interprocedural Target delivery**:

## What shapes the stacks prove, and what they do not

The DiagonalRelations admission branch accepts a concrete single-mark premise whose
output contains that same mark at STAR/MAY geometry. It stores shared FLOW geometry
and exact per-mark plain/protected memberships. This is a same-mark relation class;
it is not an ND premise-product stack. The actual premise base, field name, mark ID,
layer and H flag are not encoded in the CPU frames. Do not invent exact example
values or a static/nonstatic percentage from these stacks. Field limit 1 bounds
counted field depth, but does not bound field width, marks, contexts, relations or
subscriber counts.

The source currently restores the selected mark/class's existing diagonal rows into
a temporary TaintGroup, admits the offered facts canonically, then rewrites that
mark/class's rows only when there is a delta. Therefore even an offer with no fresh
result can perform restoration and canonical checking first. The existing typed
`addDiagonal` capability already handles some same-header/same-geometry mask admissions
without that scalar reconstruction, but completion admission calls `addAll` here.

An avoidability question is whether frequent completion offers qualify for that exact
existing direct-mask capability, with fallback for different headers/overlapping
geometry. This could avoid a reconstruction altogether rather than speed up its inner
loop. It is **not yet a selected change**: packet support, two H classes, E/tail changes,

Likewise, ordinary Target delivery should be sized from final candidate/match/fresh

subscription machinery already deduplicates admitted inputs; delivery volume does
not prove that those inputs were admitted repeatedly.

## Pinned before/after: full projection reconstruction became the default

Source comparison uses baseline `52829d5890ec3b3145cc996a1d8162d85cb8ceda` and
current `334234c24e9008f4a2614b8213b8b2e73b6ba9e1`. Exact source hashes are in
`analysis/diagonal-admission-source-comparison.json`. The broadened adapter is
introduced by implementation commit `e1838296f69ceadd04d51d0499800881bd617ff5`.

Define G as the shared geometry rows scanned in a scope. Define R as current output
path memberships represented for the selected `(scope, mark, H-class)`; P is the
number of trie nodes representing that projection. R is **not** the geometry-row
count: one row can represent a wide tree with many paths.

| Admission case | Baseline 52829 | Current 334 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Same typed header | Scan current rows and subtract their geometry from the offered delta; encode the fresh/upgrade delta only | Decode the entire selected class projection into a temporary TaintGroup, canonically admit the offer, then rewrite that class projection if fresh |
| Exact duplicate | Can discover no fresh offered geometry without materializing the complete old marked projection | Still reconstructs the complete old selected marked projection before discovering fresh is empty |
| Conflicting typed headers | Decode/reconcile through a temporary TaintGroup | Decode/reconcile through a temporary TaintGroup, as for every supported offer |

not O(1), and it has the old incompatible H-upgrade policy. The relevant difference

replacement also calls `geometry` across the retained tree. A protected decode
currently calls `scalar` for root and mask separately. These are definite source
